[spoiler=Expansion : Battle of Arxura (3,000 words approx)]The day was December 18, 1810, and the air over the small northern village of Arxura was charged with an undercurrent of palpable tension, reverberating through its narrow, cobbled streets. As snowflakes danced through the frigid air, their descent seemed almost whimsical, but the chill that settled in was not merely due to the wintry climate. It was an ominous portent of the storm about to erupt. Just beyond the distant hills, the Tarzania Independence forces, composed of thousands of brave Tarzanites, were girding themselves for a confrontation that felt both inevitable and dreadfully uncertain. They had left their homes, their families, and the warmth of loved ones behind, drawn to the call for liberation from the suffocating grip of the Holy Hydronic Empire.
Among these warriors was Arjun Malhotra, a seasoned fighter and one of the rebellions most trusted commanders. His flowing beard and weathered hands bore the marks of a life lived in struggle, yet his spirit remained unbroken. Each fighter, like Arjun, would remember the warm nights spent under the stars with loved ones, the laughter of children chasing fireflies, and the dreams of a peaceful tomorrow. Each had been awakened from slumber to join this great war for freedomto confront the Empire and reclaim what was rightfully theirs.
The village of Arxura had become more than a mere geographic point on the map; it had transformed into a stronghold for the burgeoning rebellion, a bastion of hope guarded fiercely by civilians and soldiers alike. Yet, as the minutes ticked inexorably closer to the conflict, anticipation hung thick in the air, interwoven with the fear of what awaited them in the uncertainty of destiny.
Sir, I see something on the horizon! shouted a young warrior named Rajan, his eyes wide with alarm, breaking the silence that cloaked the encampment. The urgency in his tone sparked a collective shiver among the assembled soldiers. They gazed towards the ridge, straining to discern details through the swirling snow.
A tall figure stepped forward, framed against the backdrop of a blazing sunset that painted the heavens in hues of crimson and orange. Pran Andra, the charismatic leader of the Tarzanite Rebellion, was a man of conviction. His reputation as a strategic thinker had garnered the unwavering trust of his people. As he approached Rajan, his keen eyes scanned the ridgeline.
Are those horses? Pran inquired, narrowing his gaze against the harsh lights of the dying day. The outline of armored riders began to take form, a formidable tide gathering, threatening to engulf their dreams of freedom.
Yes, sir! Hydronian cavalry! Rajan responded, the tremor in his voice betraying fear already seeping into their ranks. Pran could see the billowing plumes of dust rising from the ground, a clear indicator of the enemy's rapid approach.
Of course they are, but theyll never take this village, Pran declared with vehement conviction. He felt the mantle of leadership pressing down hard on his shoulders, not only for himself but for every Tarzanite in this struggle. The village they stood upon was not just his home but a sanctuary shared with the spirits of countless ancestors who had toiled for their livelihood. Well stand our ground!
Gathering his troops, Prans presence commanded respect, exuding strength and making their fears feel just a little less overpowering. Those soldiers up there may look fierce and intimidating, but theyll never defeat us! he proclaimed, rising upon a makeshift platform that allowed him to see all faces in the crowd, igniting inspiration and fortitude. The collective spirit of his men surged as his words pierced through their anxieties like rays of sunlight breaking through dark clouds.
They cant defeat us because we have something they dontour freedom! he shouted, and a wave of deafening cheers erupted from his comrades, echoing over the village like a powerful anthem of hope and resilience. This was no mere noise; it was a collective declaration of intent to resist, a binding that spurred them toward unyielding determination. This was their landArxuraand they would defend it with every ounce of strength they could muster.
Meanwhile, atop the hill, the Hydronian soldiers, identifiable by their distinct uniforms adorned with intricate golden patterns, displayed an unsettling calm, embodying the confidence of a well-trained army poised to showcase their might. They bore Turkish names that echoed with the pride of their imperial lineage. Their commander, General Ahmet Turgut, exuded an air of authority, directing his forces with practiced efficiency and vigilance.
Arda, prepare the artillery! he commanded with a low, commanding tone, his eyes narrowed against the setting sun as he observed the village below. His second-in-command, Arda Yilmaz, a skilled horseman with a fierce reputation, nodded with grim determination. The soldiers of the Holy Hydronic Empire were renowned for their ruthlessness, and no amount of reverie would be permitted on this day.
As the sun reached its zenith, the atmosphere shifted. At precisely 1:30 PM, the delicate silence shattered as General Turgut raised a gloved hand, signaling the charge. The command rippled through the ranksan electric energy surged, sending hundreds of horses galloping down the hill, their hooves pounding on the earth, drowning out any last echoes of hope. FOR THE EMPIRE! they cried in unison, a battle cry that rolled like thunder across the valleya proclamation of their allegiance to the imperial forces.
Ready the cannons! Pran shouted, his heart racing in rhythm with the galloping hooves of the approaching army. The scene transformed from a moment of inspiring unity to one of impending chaos as the reality of war crashed upon them. Cannons from the enemys artillery soared through the air like vengeful meteors, striking scattered homes, uprooting lives, and scattering dreams like ashes carried by the wind. The air became thick with panic as villager screams intermixed with the clash of steel and the thunder of hooves.
Pran remained resolute, fighting valiantly as he organized what remained of his troops. Regroup! Hold the line! he bellowed, his voice like a lighthouse amidst a storm, attempting to pierce through the din of chaos. But fear seeped into their ranks like a noxious gas, overwhelming his orders as the Hydronians pressed forward with unrelenting power. The disciplined nature of the Imperial forces became undeniable, sweeping through the Tarzanite lines like a tempest.
Amid the chaos, Arjun Malhotra fought fiercely in the midst of the melee, rallying his comrades as he swung his sword, determined to defend not only the land but also the very essence of their struggle. Turning to fellow fighters, he shouted, Forget the fear! Fight for your homes, for your families! We shall not submit!
Around him, young soldierslike the eager and impulsive Rajanresponded to his fiery call. Rajan stood shoulder to shoulder with Arjun, his heart racing. With each clash of steel and each cry of defiance resonating in his ears, a sense of purpose surged through him. For Arxura! he yelled, his voice laced with fervor as he engaged in battle. Each strike of his sword mirrored the heartbeat of his village, a pulse of defiance that refused to be silenced.
Yet the gravity of their numbers overwhelmed them; the Hydronian soldiers advanced relentlessly, like a tide crashing over the shore, leaving despair in their wake. Gunfire roared, silencing voices that even months before filled the air with laughter and song. With every soldier lost, the memory of a beloved family member turned into only echoes of grief that clung to Arjuns heart like a relentless shadow.
Just as he turned to urge Rajan to seize the moment, gunfire erupted in a thunderous crack. A bullet struck Arjuns shoulder, the pain a sharp reminder of the fragile line between life and death. He stumbled; his determination faltered momentarily as agony flared through him.
Arjun! Rajan shouted, his face pale with horror. He rushed to his commanders side, fear catching his breath. Stay with me! We need you!
Im fine, Arjun gasped through clenched teeth, holding his bloody shoulder, wincing with each movement. We must keep fighting. Protect the village.
But as he looked around, panic surged in his chestmany of his comrades were falling, overwhelmed by the barrage of the Hydronian onslaught, swords clashing with merciless fury. Lives snuffed out like candles in the wind, the once-vibrant village dissolving into a landscape of death, chaos, and smoke.
Determined, Pran fought beside Arjun and Rajan, his sword a blur as he fought with an unshakeable resolve, calling to the remaining Tarzanites. These are our lands! Stand strong! Well face them together! His voice remained a beacon, though the defeat threatened to seep into the hearts of his comrades like a bitter chill.
As dusk settled over the battlefield, the faint light of day painted shadows that danced over the remnants of what had once been a proud village, alive with laughter and warmth. Now, it lay in ruins, a graveyard of dreams that smouldered in grim silence. The only sounds that echoed amongst the debris and wreckage were the expressions of pure despair accompanying those who had fought for their freedom.
One soldier, a young woman named Priya, bolted from the shadows, her heart beating wildly as she took in the carnage surrounding her. She had been entrusted with tending to the wounded, her skills as a healer honed by necessity. The screams of the injured called out to her as she moved swiftly through the carnage. Stay with me! Keep breathing! she urged to a man she knew had fought bravely alongside her. She applied pressure to his wound, her hands trembling but her mind resolute. You are strong; you can pull through!
But the souls lost to the fire of battle were countless, and the weight of loss threaded its way into the hearts of those who remained, seeping darkness into their courage.
Meanwhile, General Turgut surveyed the scene from atop his horse, a cold glint in his eyes. He was a man forged by ambition and power, possessing little regard for loss. Push forward! Crush their resistance! he barked his orders, dismissing the plight of the dying as he sought more glory for the Empire.
Arda, his second-in-command, watched his commander with a blend of admiration and growing trepidation. As a battle-hardened soldier, he understood the weight of leadership but also felt the tide of soldiers lives spilling onto the ground beneath him. Each fallen Tarzanite represented not just a statistic but a story, a heartbeat, a family. General, Arda hesitated, seeking a moment to voice his concerns. Were fighting against men whove bled for their causedo we not respect that?
Respect? General Turgut scoffed, the word tinged with disdain. They are merely rebels, pawns in a game they do not understand. Show them no mercy, Arda; this is war!
Bitter conflict surged within Arda as he watched the Hydronians push forward, trampling dreams beneath their boots, the cries of the wounded haunting him. He knew that every choice would lead to deeper consequences, ones that would echo long after the dust settled.
In that moment of reflection, Arda felt a flicker of conscience ignite within him. No more, Turgut! he declared, his voice firm, garnering curiosity from the soldiers around them. We must show restraint; we cannot simply conquer through destruction!
Yet, as he faced Turgut, he knew the resolve of his commander was unyielding. Restraint is a luxury we cannot afford! the general replied, his gaze icy. Do you want to live in chains? Do you want to be bowing to this rabble for the rest of your life?
The soft tension morphed into a violent clash, but Arda clenched his fists, drawing strength from the maelstrom around him. I want to live in honor, Ahmet! I want to leave a legacy that doesnt require blood as currency!
But Turgut remained unmoved; instead, he drew his sword, glaring with a promise that shattered any remaining vestiges of doubt. Then choose your side, he spat, anger simmering in his voice.
Meanwhile, the battlefield raged ona horror show that melded into a nightmarish vision of chaos. Prans voice echoed across the tumult, urging his men to hold the line as waves of Hydronian soldiers surged toward them with unyielding fervor.
FOR ARXURA! Pran yelled, a rallying cry that propelled the Tarzanites forward, channeling their fear into determination.
Yet the tide of war turned crueler still, with bodies littering the ground as the sun began to dip below the horizon. The screams of the injured punctuated the air, a violent symphony underscoring the grim reality unfolding around them.
Amidst the chaos, Priya moved like a ghost between fighters, tending to the fallen with a heavy heart. Every life that slipped away from her grasp twisted her insides with guilt and sorrow. Two children, whose laughter had once echoed through the village, lay lifeless, their innocence extinguished far too soon. Tears streamed down Priyas cheeks as she fought to save those still breathing.
In a moment of desolation, Rajan stumbled back, bloodied from the combat and trembling with horror. He turned to Arjun, fear-filled eyes searching for answers. What do we do now? he asked, the panic threading through his voice, raw and real.
We fight, Arjun responded fiercely, even as the weight of exhaustion threatened to crush him beneath its burden. We may fall, but we wont surrender! Our familiesour futuredepends on this. For every one of us they take down, a thousand will rise in our place!
But just then, Pran noticed something flashing in the darkness, a small glimmer hidden among the rubble. He moved toward it and found a shard of an old mirror that had belied the history of the village. The reflection caught his attentionnot his own, but memories of laughter, prosperity, and unity. He raised the shard high for all to see, its surface delivering a picture of forgotten dreams and resilience.
This is not just a battle for survival; its a battle for our very souls! Pran expressed vehemently, holding the shard aloft. We cannot let them steal our spirit!
The rallying cry surged through the Tarzanite ranks, igniting a fire in their bellies as they summoned the strength to fight. Yet, the onslaught from the Hydronian cavalry surged forward like a relentless tide.
As night fell, the battlefield transformed into an eerie landscape, illuminated by the dim light of dying fires set against the inky darkness. In this morbid twilight, Rajans resolve solidified; he stepped forward alongside Arjun, feeling the weight of history rest heavily on his shoulders.
Together! Arjun shouted, a fierce light igniting within his core.
And with that, the renewed strength surged through the Tarzanites, pushing back against the Hydronians with furious resolve, strikes cutting through the shadow of despair that threatened to swallow them whole.
Yet, amidst it all, the chaos raged, the war continued without pause. As the battle reached its climax, Priya stumbled upon Arjun, who had fallen against a stone wall, exhausted and wounded but still fiery in spirit. We cant lose hope! she exclaimed, rushing to his side, cradling him as he fought against unconsciousness.
Not so long as we breathe, he whispered, his voice shaking with agony yet rife with determination. Keep going, Priya. They can take our flesh but not our freedom.
And as if her words had the power to alter destiny, the tide began to turn. The Tarzanites banded together, forcing the Hydronian soldiers back, slicing through their ranks. General Turguts fury boiled over; he raised his sword, urging his troops forward with a savage battle cry, but even as they pushed, the human will proved to be an unbreakable force.
Arda Yilmaz felt the rush of impending doom wash over him as he witnessed the tides shifting. In that moment of conflict, he decided to step forward, turning away from the Empires destructive path. Enough! he shouted, no longer hidden behind Turguts shadow. This is not what we fight for! We are men, not monsters! The world deserves better than this!
The clamor of battle stilled momentarily as soldiers drifted in confusion, both Tarzanites and Hydronians alike glancing toward Arda, uncertainty etched into their faces.
Turgut whipped around, furious at this mutiny. You dare question my command? he thundered, raising his weapon threateningly.
I dare, Arda asserted, standing his ground, a mix of fear and conviction anchoring him. In this chaos, we lose our humanity, our honor. What victory lies in destroying their spirit?
As Ardas plea rang through the air, Pran seized the moment. Yes! Were not enemies! Our homes may be divided, our loyalties challenged, but we share this earth! We fight for a future our children can inherit without sorrow!
The words echoed, deepening in weight as they crossed the battlefield. For the first time, soldiers of both social classes stopped and considered the motives driving each other. Bonds formed in the face of death. Fear turned to compassion as the larger questions of legacy and morality arose amidst the bloodshed.
And then, like a rampaging river breaking a dam, the call for peace reverberated through the fighters, spilling over a bridge of understanding that may have once seemed insurmountable.
Lay down your weapons! Arda shouted, seriousness igniting his fiercely noble heart. Life is worth more than any conquest! His eyes caught Prans, an unspoken understanding lingering between them as they shared in the weight of their words.
Arjun looked at Rajan, confusion, anger, and determination swirling in the depths of their souls. We either continue this bloodbath or embrace a chance at peace.
And one by one, like withered leaves falling from trees in autumn, soldiers dropped their swords, letting them clatter to the ground. Broken and exhausted, they came together as men and womenneighbors, families, and friends, relinquishing the need for violence.
Turgut, blinded by arrogance and fury, charged towards Arda. You traitor! he shouted, but the rest of the soldiers formed an unwilling phalanx before him, and he skidded to a halt.
Enough! Stand down, General! Arda commanded, aiming his weapon towards Turgut, who found himself flanked by soldiers previously loyal. This is our moment to break the cycle!
Frozen in place and faced by the unexpected rebellion, Turgut faltered, rage and disbelief playing across his face. He lowered his weapon but refused to yield, embers of fury smoldering in his eyes.
And in that moment of collective vulnerability, a new resolution formed among the Tarzanites and Hydronians alike. Through the pain, they had found a shared language, a collective understanding of shared existence beyond imperial power and the fight for territory.
The first snowflakes of winter drifted gently down from the heavens, ignoring the clash of history, softening the remnants of conflict that marked the battlefield. As the shadows of the past lifted, a new light began to dawna light promising hope and possibility.
I propose a truce, Pran declared, stepping forward to extend his hand towards Arda, who met him halfway, their shared dignity binding them in solidarity. We can build anewon the ashes of an old war. Let us forge a future with a new beginning, hand in hand!
Arda nodded, his heart brimming with the hope that had ignited within their rallying spirit. Together, we can create a foundation that our children will build upon; we must find a way to heal the wounds of this land.
And as the remaining soldiers looked on, they saw not enemies before them but fellow humans, each grappling with the weight of their choices, faces softened by mutual respect.
And so it was that amidst the scars of conflict, forgiveness wove its way through their hearts, resolutely reestablishing a shared identity. Though the battleground lay littered with the remnants of conflict, the promise of a new dawn glimmered on the horizon.
The struggle had not ended without pain, but what emerged from the dusk of war was the essence of the human spiritthe conviction to coexist, to honor the lives lost, and to pledge never to walk the path of violence again.
Freed from the shackles of their past, a new chapter would unfoldone rich with possibility, nourished by the lessons learned upon the battlefield of Arxura.
As the sun set low, casting golden rays upon the scars of the earth, Pran and Arda forged a bond that mirrored the unbreakable resilience of their people. Hope prevailed, rising like the phoenix from the ashes, heralding a tomorrow marked not by dominance but by unity that transcended all boundaries.
In the heart of every Tarzanite and Hydronian, a new narrative began to take shape: one not of conquest but of collaboration; one driven by freedom and respect for humanity rather than mere dominance.
From that day forward, the village of Arxura would not just be remembered as the site of a fierce battle but also as the crucible where a new destiny was forged in the fires of conflicta legacy for future generations, echoing with an unwavering pledge: to fight for a world where peace and freedom prevailed.
And somewhere in the quiet of that moonlit night, the seeds of resilience were firmly planted in the soil of their hearts, poised to blossom into a kaleidoscope of hopea vibrant testament that love, compassion, and unity could transcend all, shining a light into the darkest corners of their shared destinies.

[i][b]First Contact[/b]
[sub]Caprium, Versia
Late Mar 2025[/sub]

I stood upon a cliff edge, possibly in the cold mountain ranges just north of Mineros. Before me were thousands upon thousands of stormtroopers, each looking to the nation of [nation]Akhratia[/nation], our neutral northern neighbor. The Aquilius feathers on my soldiers' helms fluttered gracefully in the wind. As I unsheathed my sword to give the advance, an arrow flew through the air, striking the ground only a few inches from my sandals. The stone beneath me crumbled and gave way, sending me into blackness. Falling into a seemlessly endless pit, my anxiety grew and grew until I hit the hard ground. I felt no pain, but I could barely make out the outline of my Imperial Throne as I crawled to it, yet my vision faded. There was no sound except my labored breathing. That too, also faded.

I awoke in a state of delusion, only to realize I was in the Imperial Court, atop of that same iron throne in my dream. Adjutant Asseylum Vers Allusia, a relative of mine but also one of my closest friends, tapped my shoulder.

"My Rex, you live to see another day. I was beginning to think you weren't going to wake up at all! it seems I worried for nothing." At least she cared. After the Great Versian Civil War (1975 - 2016) and my father's betrayal and murder (2011), I had stripped the Versian nobility of their titles and pegged them down to Economic Barons, which decreased their standing with me significantly. Likewise, the peasants of Versia hate me also, for burning down their Kingdom in the name of Justice afore the war ended. I am viewed as a Tyrant, like my Father before me. Yet, I am revered, as my subjects are too powerless to resist my iron grip. Yet, despite all this, my Adjutant remained loyal to my cause, and stayed by my side to this very day.

"What's the meaning of this, you disrupt my slumber, again? I was just getting to the good part!" Asseylum knew I was teasing, yet didn't give me an answer to my complaining, rather, she motioned for the Sentinels to open the Iron Door (a giant, towering, highly-detailed iron door with depictions of previous Emperors engraved upon it), and it slowly slid open as my third cousin, Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia, a fickle Bureaucrat under the service of the Adjutant, was ushered forward with haste. He prostrated himself before me. 

"My glorious Rex, may you live forever! I have answered your summons and have traveled here from Iuvavum, as you have commanded." 

"Good. I have a top-secret mission for you, and you will do exactly as I say!" Julius' face remained low as I assigned him with the task of introducing ourselves to [nation=noflag+long]The Crystalline Empire[/nation].

"...and then, you will stay for however long they need you. Remember, no one other than us must know what you're up to, or they must be eliminated silently. These plans must be kept quiet until you reach your destination. Or maybe this will be your first and last assignment?!" I gave Julius a hard stare, while he avoided making eye contact. "Any questions? No? Good! Off you go, then. I entrust this great task of bringing our glorious nation from the darkness of Isolationism into your [b]capable[/b] hands." I murmered a Latin prayer under my breath as he hurried away with a telegram, written in my own words, in hand. An armored car bearing the Versian insignia awaited Julius at the front gates, upon which he entered the vehicle and sped away from the Capital.

[quote=versia;58959165][i][b]First Contact[/b]
[sub]Caprium, Versia
Late Mar 2025[/sub]

I stood upon a cliff edge, possibly in the cold mountain ranges just north of Mineros. Before me were thousands upon thousands of stormtroopers, each looking to the nation of [nation]Akhratia[/nation], our neutral northern neighbor. The Aquilius feathers on my soldiers' helms fluttered gracefully in the wind. As I unsheathed my sword to give the advance, an arrow flew through the air, striking the ground only a few inches from my sandals. The stone beneath me crumbled and gave way, sending me into blackness. Falling into a seemlessly endless pit, my anxiety grew and grew until I hit the hard ground. I felt no pain, but I could barely make out the outline of my Imperial Throne as I crawled to it, yet my vision faded. There was no sound except my labored breathing. That too, also faded.

I awoke in a state of delusion, only to realize I was in the Imperial Court, atop of that same iron throne in my dream. Adjutant Asseylum Vers Allusia, a relative of mine but also one of my closest friends, tapped my shoulder.

"My Rex, you live to see another day. I was beginning to think you weren't going to wake up at all! it seems I worried for nothing." At least she cared. After the Great Versian Civil War (1975 - 2016) and my father's betrayal and murder (2011), I had stripped the Versian nobility of their titles and pegged them down to Economic Barons, which decreased their standing with me significantly. Likewise, the peasants of Versia hate me also, for burning down their Kingdom in the name of Justice afore the war ended. I am viewed as a Tyrant, like my Father before me. Yet, I am revered, as my subjects are too powerless to resist my iron grip. Yet, despite all this, my Adjutant remained loyal to my cause, and stayed by my side to this very day.

"What's the meaning of this, you disrupt my slumber, again? I was just getting to the good part!" Asseylum knew I was teasing, yet didn't give me an answer to my complaining, rather, she motioned for the Sentinels to open the Iron Door (a giant, towering, highly-detailed iron door with depictions of previous Emperors engraved upon it), and it slowly slid open as my third cousin, Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia, a fickle Bureaucrat under the service of the Adjutant, was ushered forward with haste. He prostrated himself before me. 

"My glorious Rex, may you live forever! I have answered your summons and have traveled here from Iuvavum, as you have commanded." 

"Good. I have a top-secret mission for you, and you will do exactly as I say!" Julius' face remained low as I assigned him with the task of introducing ourselves to [nation=noflag+long]The Crystalline Empire[/nation].

"...and then, you will stay for however long they need you. Remember, no one other than us must know what you're up to, or they must be eliminated silently. These plans must be kept quiet until you reach your destination. Or maybe this will be your first and last assignment?!" I gave Julius a hard stare, while he avoided making eye contact. "Any questions? No? Good! Off you go, then. I entrust this great task of bringing our glorious nation from the darkness of Isolationism into your [b]capable[/b] hands." I murmered a Latin prayer under my breath as he hurried away with a telegram, written in my own words, in hand. An armored car bearing the Versian insignia awaited Julius at the front gates, upon which he entered the vehicle and sped away from the Capital.
[/i][/quote]

[b]The visitor[/b]
Driving from Vers to the capital city of Thýven perhaps was a lovely experience, as the dense forest at the Versian-Thýven border gave way to low lying farm plains and small quaint villages. There would be no major cities along this route which was highly rural and underdeveloped, aside from the rail-lines which occasionally flirted with the road, following it for a few seconds before seemingly leaping away behind some low hillock. The figures in the fields were antlered and seemed to be male, resembling deer bucks, while those without antlers were clearly female. The fashion out here was clearly simpler, the women wore colorful patterned dresses with simple blouses, the men usually some rustic colored overalls with a white shirt or a decorated shirt, usually with a wide brimmed hat. Indeed perhaps a question would arise from the figure who was in the car as if the nation was even modernised, the answer of course, would be given as in the distance tall cell-towers loomed over the horizon in neat rows. 

The approach to the capital city was one of gradual order, with the fields giving way to clean suburbs (though these were more akin to small villages that had been build around the city) before finally reaching the first outer ring of the city, which was demarcated by a wide 20 foot canal that went around the cities outer star-shaped historic wall. The gates of the city, which bore the name of the city, Throgar , some strange name whose meaning had been lost to time. 

The city was neat and orderly, quaint two story houses with wrought iron balconies and large old oak doors stood in the outer ring, before giving way to larger more austere, and clearly more historic houses of brick, and stone, with heavy shutters which seemed to shout dignity and wealth lives here. The city was designed in a radial pattern, expanding out from the port which faced the White Sea, all roads would connect to the main square which was less of a square and more of a basin lined with government buildings and two grand roads that separated them from the water, which was lined with steps into the water, with the entrance  to the basin being crowned by two 300 foot tall stone statues of two male Thrømm figures, their antlers curving gracefully into the sky. 

Given the fact that Julius Valerian Cassiodorus Vers Allusia wouldve had to undergo some form of border crossing, even if minimal on the side of Thýven and Versia, his presence wouldve been noted, and the arrival of the car in the capital wouldve been already reported to the right authorities, for the Thrømm are precise in this nature. As a result the car, having made its way to the palace, which was located to the East side of this grand basin at the end of a long road, a humble three story dwelling, with a design that seemed to mix italian renaissance of Venice with that of Neo-Classical elegance, with vines crawling over its face, and joyful dark green shutters hung before the windows. A small courtyard would face the cross-street and Julius would be permitted into the sight of an elderly female deer waiting in the tall doorway of the palace, which really on the outside did not resemble a palace but the manor of a noble.

[b]Establishment of the Erene Economic and Humanitarian Pact (EEHP)[/b]

[i]Today the Minister of the United Lavian Republic is sending out a call for a economic pact spanning the world to not only better connect the nations of Erene, but to also help deny monetary or political gain to those who violate human rights and suppress their people. This pact looks to help better connect the world economically and ethically through the following points, to be made clear or adjusted once nations have adequately joined and the debate process can begin, with a set of ground principals to base off of:[/i]

[b]1. Open borders and ports:[/b] The members of the EEHP will share open borders with each other. In practice, this means citizens of each nation will have the privilege of traveling passport and visa free, with the potential of streamlined immigration between members. This brings the benefit of increased tourism and a larger sense of collaboration between members. Members will also have open port policies with the other members, meaning a decrease in docking fees allowing for ease of business between members.

[b]2. Sharing of business licenses and integration of international safety standards:[/b]Members of the EEHP will share the same level of safety standards and regulations, thus allowing for companies to be licensed in one country and use that license across all nations in the EEHP rather than having to get multiple licenses and concern themselves with different laws and safety standards. This will not only help companies, but also ensure that ethical practices in EEHP countries will be encouraged.

[b]3. Sharing of innovations and breakthroughs:[/b] EEHP members will share practices with each other to not only benefit members, but also build a better Erene for current and future generations. This includes the sharing of the best industry practices to prevent environmental impact via pollution, deforestation, over-farming/fishing, and also share stake in world wide conservation projects of natural habitats and cultural sites. Breakthroughs in industries will also be shared between nations, allowing for better industry practices across the world.

[b]4. Implement tariffs and import restrictions on nations that promote unethical practices or undemocratic principals:[/b] Membership in the EEHP not only looks to benefit the nations in it, but to benefit the world via lowering and hopefully removing reliance on fascist nations or those ruled by dictators (not including constitutional monarchies, parliamentary monarchies, or similar governments that practice the basics of democracy and good humanitarian practices.) Stemming the reliance on child labor and the exploitation of workers via taxing the imports from these nations will hopefully encourage the nations that use these practices to pivot to more sustainable and humanitarian based practices. The first and second points of this charter will also help ease the transition from the companies that use these practices by making the shipment of resources between members cheaper and more accessible to companies in the member nations.

[b]5. Promotion of humanitarian practices:[/b] Humanitarian laws to be practiced and imposed in member nations include but are not limited to: 
- Laws against exclusion of people based on their race, gender, sexuality, or religion
- Freedom of religion
- Freedom of speech (specifics to be determined by the founding members)
- Minimum wage laws (to be determined by the individual country)
- Limit on maximum hours of work before overtime pay begins
- Free school for at least up until grade/year 8 in less developed countries, and free high school for the more developed countries (university/college is up to the individual country to decide)
These policies will be helped via an aid fund to be contributed to by each government via a number of % of their GDP to help other member nations with disasters or modernization

Invited members include:
[nation]Indonocaismnic[/nation]
[nation]Sikirsk[/nation]
[nation]United Hydronia[/nation]
[nation]New Westmore[/nation]
[nation]Goleornacha Roleplay Posts[/nation]
Membership is not restricted to these nations and the ULR encourages people to apply for membership, this list is simply a list of countries the ULR knows are respectable and has good relations with already. It should also be clarified that this will not interject with any military alliances, however if one member attacks another, or a nation attacks a member and another member state joins the attack, the attacking member will be removed from the pact if the member does not provide ample reason for such action.
